subject: Recap: Code Mode for Extensible Software (AI That Works Session)
body:
Hello First Name,

Our latest 🦄 ai that works session was all about "Code Mode for Extensible Software." We explored how it helps AI agents become much more capable!

You can find the full recording, code, and diagrams from the session on GitHub here:
https://github.com/hellovai/ai-that-works

We dove deep into Code Mode, looking at its practical applications and what it means for the future of extensible AI agents. Here's a quick rundown:

*   **Beyond Simple Tool Calls:** Code Mode allows AI agents to write and run code (like JavaScript or Bash) to chain, pipe, and process tools. This makes complex, multi-step operations much more efficient than just sequential LLM tool calls.
*   **Tackling Scale & Speed:** This is key for situations with many tools, dynamic tool discovery, and needing operations to run at "code speed." It helps prevent latency and outdated data, especially in real-time, multi-user environments.
*   **Secure & Type-Safe Extensibility:** We explored how to build solid Code Mode systems using sandboxed runtimes (like QuickJS with custom bindings) for untrusted code. We also covered advanced techniques such as embedded compilers for compile-time type safety, memory limits, and I/O overrides.

If there's one key takeaway from the session, it's this:
Code Mode changes AI agents from basic tool-callers into smart workflow composers. This gives them incredible flexibility and efficiency, letting them tap into existing code ecosystems, all while maintaining strong security and type-safety.

Got questions? Just reply to this email or ask on Discord: https://www.boundaryml.com/discord. We read every message! Happy coding 🧑‍💻

Vaibhav & Dex
